tasks.description: New module src/io/browser/ (a long-lived service like mcp_client, not a one-shot tool function): a BrowserSession manager holding ONE shared thirtyfour session driven over WebDriver BiDi (WebDriver::bidi(), caps.enable_bidi()), spawned via tokio::process::Command following the mcp_client precedent (TokioChildProcess-style lifecycle), with start/stop/restart and recovery if geckodriver dies. The session subscribes to BiDi events (navigation committed/failed, load, dialogs, console/log) so the agent reacts to pushed events instead of polling. Classic WebDriver methods on the same session remain the fallback for anything BiDi does not cover. Profile dir comes from config (see task 353). Shutdown on Helix stop must quit the driver cleanly (no orphan geckodriver/firefox processes). SINGLE-SESSION RULE (BiDi): Firefox allows exactly ONE BiDi session and it outlives its WebSocket - always call session.end on shutdown; if a client dies without ending it, Firefox refuses new sessions until restarted, so on startup a refused session means restart Firefox (do not retry the same session). EVOLUTION SEAM: keep all BiDi usage behind a thin isolated layer inside src/io/browser/ (e.g. a bidi.rs module) - the rest of the browser module talks to the seam, not directly to thirtyfour's BiDi types - so spec and Firefox updates are cheap to absorb. And the Phase 3 PR path (task 290) is queue-only - QueueBackend appends to rt/self_improve/pr_queue.jsonl and no GitHub call happens in-crate, ever; there is NO queue consumer anywhere in the codebase, so even with pr_opening on, a payload would sit in the queue forever. Decision: a DEDICATED narrow push op in the loop's git wrapper - NOT the shell tool. The shell tool is general-purpose with only a substring denylist and cannot enforce branch/target rules; a dedicated op enforces by construction, like the rest of the wrapper. Rule: push ONLY the evaluated/promoted branch, ONLY to origin, refspec HEAD:refs/heads/<branch> with the branch name validated (self-improve/<slug>, same safe-branch-name rules), never --force, never --tags, never master or PreRelese as the push target (the PR target is PreRelese; the push target is the feature branch). Uses the existing R630 SSH deploy key - no new secret, no credential helper, no HTTPS token. Gated by the Phase 3 gate (task 290): push happens only when the gate passes (promoted plus eval green plus clean audit plus eval_set_approved plus target PreRelese); while pr_opening is false, no push happens, same as today. The evaluator currently deletes the worktree plus branch after evaluation whether it passes or fails - this task must preserve the promoted branch (skip deletion on promotion) so there is something to push. PR opening stays with the queue consumer (external - Cobble jr opens PRs via the GitHub connector today, same as Ranger PRs); the loop never calls merge_pull_request.
tasks.details: Extend validate_argv with a narrow push shape (push origin <branch>, exactly, no flags); pin the remote to origin; pin cwd by the worktree-root parent rule; SSH auth via the R630's existing SSH config (do not strip SSH_AUTH_SOCK / HOME in a way that breaks the deploy key - verify). Add tests mirroring the existing rejection table (push to master, push --force, push --tags, push to a non-origin remote, push of a branch outside self-improve/ - all rejected). Branch preservation: evaluator keeps the promoted branch plus worktree until the push succeeds, then cleans up; a failed push leaves the branch in place with a log line, never a silent drop.

Do NOT touch the `chat` arm's auth status - the ungated `chat` arm is John's decided product choice.

tasks.title: H3: Retry policy can't survive real Starlink drops — shared retry_with_backoff helper
tasks.description: Helix triple review H3 (Claude + Grok). Ollama uses a fixed 2.5s delay and Gemini 2s then 4s, giving up after ~5-6s; call_gemini_direct and the OKF fetcher have limited/no retry; IMAP has no retry at all. Fix: one shared retry_with_backoff helper with jittered exponential backoff (~2s rising to a 60s cap, ~5 attempts), honouring Retry-After on 429/503 and failing fast on other 4xx. Wire it into the Ollama + Gemini per-round calls, call_gemini_direct, the OKF fetcher, and the IMAP connect.
tasks.results: Done 2026-11-19 (branch ranger-helix-h3h4h5): shared retry_with_backoff helper in src/io/retry.rs (jittered exponential backoff 2s -> 60s cap, 5 attempts, Retry-After honoured on 429/503, fail-fast on other 4xx) wired into Ollama + Gemini per-round calls, call_gemini, OKF fetcher, and IMAP connect. Full cargo +1.99 test suite green: 1601 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored (lib 783/0/6, bin helix 758/0/6, bin installer 24/0/0, integration 35/0/0, doctests 1/0/1). 8 retry-helper unit tests pass.
tasks.details: New module src/io/retry.rs: RetryPolicy (max_attempts 5, base 2000ms, cap 60000ms), exponential_delay_ms (pure, exact), backoff_delay (jittered, +0-25%), retry_after (parses Retry-After seconds, capped; HTTP-date form falls back to backoff), delay_for_response (Retry-After wins, else backoff), is_retryable_status (429/503/5xx only), is_retryable_reqwest_error (timeout/connect), RetryError enum (Retryable{source, delay} / Fatal), async retry_with_backoff driver + sync retry_with_backoff_sync driver. Wired into: Ollama call_ollama_tools per-round HTTP call, Gemini call_gemini_tools per-round HTTP call, call_gemini (single-shot, used by call_gemini_direct + call_gemini_sync), OKF fetcher fetch_manifest/fetch_knowledge/health_check (304 treated as a valid response for conditional requests), IMAP imap_connect (sync retry of TCP connect + TLS handshake; login done once, not retried, so a bad-password failure cannot lock the account). Note: the only proper exponential backoff in the tree was in io/ollama/keepalive.rs, which L5 flagged as undeclared/uncompiled — that was already fixed by PR #49 (keepalive is now a declared module and wired up), so no L5 work here.

tasks.title: Nightly network report: no 24h monitoring history exists (scheduled capture logger)
tasks.description: Task 375 gave the chat-command loop live wire tools (mcp__wire__capture/interfaces/analyze_pcap in the read allowlist), so the nightly network report can now be grounded in a live capture + interfaces instead of refused. But no 24h archive exists anywhere: the Nov 17 continuous monitor never persisted, and no code runs captures on a schedule and stores summaries. A report built after 375 is a live snapshot, not 24h of history. Build a scheduled capture logger so the nightly report can summarize the last 24h: a Helix routine (or equivalent scheduled job) that runs an mcp_wire capture periodically and appends a compact summary line (time, interface, packet/error/retransmission/drop counts, latency notes) to a runtime log file the loop's read_log can read; the report task then reads the last 24h of that log.
tasks.details: Design first (376.1): where the log lives (runtime logs dir, so read_log can reach it — it already rejects dotdot/symlink escapes, so keep the file under logs/), cadence (hourly is plenty for a nightly verdict; every 60s like the old monitor is overkill for a file), retention/rotation (cap the file — a 24h window is ~24 lines at hourly cadence; do not let it grow unbounded), and line format (one compact line per capture: timestamp, interface, counts). Implementation (376.2): the scheduled job + the capture call + the append (direct exec via the existing mcp_wire capture path, not a new shell); keep it read-only (observe traffic, modify nothing) and fail-soft (a missed capture logs a warning, never breaks Helix). Out of scope: do NOT reintroduce write:chat; the report still comes back to the command room and Cobble jr relays it. This is an enhancement on top of 375, not a fix for a refusal — the report works as a snapshot without it. 376.1 DESIGN (recorded 2026-11-20): Log = <runtime>/logs/network_capture.log (under logs/ so read_log can read it as logs/network_capture.log; read_log serves only logs/, rejects dotdot/symlink escapes, and returns at most the last 2000 chars). Cadence = hourly via seeded cron routine 'network-capture-log' (schedule 'every 1h', enabled by default); legacy in-process handler (empty task, like support-mail-watch/chat-command-watch) — no LLM is spawned to poll; the cron load_or_seed merge carries the seed to older deployments. Capture = per tick call mcp__wire__interfaces, pick the primary interface (first non-loopback, operstate up, IPv4 address, preferring a LAN-range IPv4 192.168/10/172.16-31), then call mcp__wire__capture {interface, count 50, duration_secs 10} (10s sample); both calls via existing mcp_client::try_execute on a blocking thread with a 60s timeout — no new shell, no new subprocess. Summary = parse the capture JSON; pkts = captured count; count packet info-column substrings: retr = 'Retransmission', rst = '[RST', dupack = 'Dup ACK', ooo = 'Out-Of-Order'. True interface error/drop counters are NOT available from the wire tools (interfaces returns no statistics) — the line records only what a live capture can observe and does not fabricate error/drop numbers. Line format (one compact line, ~60 chars, whitespace-split parseable): '2026-11-21T05:00:00 ens18 pkts=14 retr=0 rst=0 dupack=0 ooo=0' (local ISO timestamp, no spaces). Retention = cap 48 lines (48h at hourly cadence); on append, drop oldest lines and keep the last 48; file stays ~3KB so read_log's 2000-char tail covers ~33 lines (>24h). Fail-soft = any failure (MCP disabled, no wire server, no usable interface, capture timeout/error, unparseable JSON, append failure) logs a warning to the error log and returns; a missed capture appends nothing (archive holds only real samples; gaps in timestamps are visible to the report). 376.2 IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-20 (branch ranger-helix-task376-build): new src/network_capture.rs (summarize_capture, pick_primary_interface with LAN preference, format_capture_line, append_capture_line capped at 48, run_capture_cycle via mcp_client::try_execute on a blocking thread with timeouts); Cpu::routine_network_capture_log + dispatch arm in handle_routine_run; seeded routine network-capture-log (every 1h, enabled) in cron/registry.rs with load_or_seed merge; mod declared in both src/lib.rs and src/main.rs (bin has its own mod list — the full suite caught the missing bin declaration); docs/chat-command-loop.md §7 + CHANGELOG Added section. Full cargo +1.99 test green: 1637 passed / 0 failed / 13 ignored (lib 801/0/6, bin helix 776/0/6, installer 24/0/0, integration 35, doctests 1/0/1). 376.3 live drill is John's R630 step (log accumulates over several hours, then a ! llm report task summarises the last 24h from the log).

tasks.title: H8: Shell denylist bypass via ;/&&/| command chaining
tasks.description: The shell tool's denylist can be bypassed by chaining a blocked command after an allowed one (e.g. `allowed; blocked` or `allowed && blocked`). Root cause: check_shell_argv0 (src/tools/shell_security.rs) only analysed the FIRST command's argv[0], and the substring denylist does not cover the generalised cases (rm -rf $HOME, dd of=/dev/<anything>). So `echo ok; rm -rf $HOME` passed both layers. Fix: split the command into segments at unquoted ;/&&/||/|/&/newline (quoting honoured) and run the argv[0] analysis on EVERY segment; the substring layer stays whole-string.
tasks.details: 384.1 SPEC/REPRO: seams are validate_shell_command / check_shell_argv0 (src/tools/shell_security.rs), called from run_shell (src/tools/shell_tool.rs:100). The argv[0] layer tokenized the whole command and only checked words[0] (after sudo/env wrappers); the substring layer has no patterns for `rm -rf $HOME` or `dd of=/dev/<anything>`. Repro (all passed validation on unhardened code): `echo ok; rm -rf $HOME`, `echo ok && rm -rf ${HOME}`, `ls && dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/vda`, `echo hi | dd of=/dev/vda`, `echo ok\nrm -rf $HOME`. 384.2 IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-25 (branch ranger-helix-h8, rebased onto origin/PreRelese ba28cb2 first): new split_command_segments() splits at unquoted `;`, `&`, `|`, newline, respecting single quotes, double quotes, and backslash escapes (quotes kept in segments so shell_word_split sees exact text); `&&`/`||`/`;;` yield empty segments, harmless. validate_shell_command now runs check_shell_argv0 on every segment; substring layer unchanged. 3 new tests (chained-denied-segments, benign-chaining-and-quoted-denied-text, splitter unit test). Known limits (out of scope, noted for follow-up): command substitution $(...) and backticks are NOT unpacked (pre-existing documented limit); subshell-wrapped denied commands `(rm -rf $HOME)` and `time`-prefixed commands are adjacent bypass classes. 384.3 VERIFY: new chaining test confirmed FAILING on unhardened code first (`echo ok; rm -rf $HOME` passed validation) and passing after. tasks.title: H9: Background children escape the shell timeout (pipe stays open forever)
tasks.description: spawn_and_wait (src/tools/shell_tool.rs:268-289) and run_command_with_timeout (src/chat_command/executor.rs:172-195) already put the child in its own process group and SIGKILL the group on timeout, but the drain threads are joined with an unbounded join(). A background child keeps the stdout pipe open, so `sleep 99999 &` (sh exits at once, orphaned sleep inherits stdout) blocks out_handle.join() forever and the shell timeout never fires; a setsid'd child escapes the group kill too, so the timeout path hangs the same way. Fix: kill the process group after reaping (a Job Object on Windows) and join the drain threads with a deadline so a background child cannot hold the pipe open past the timeout.
tasks.details: 385.1 SPEC/REPRO: seams are spawn_and_wait (src/tools/shell_tool.rs, unbounded join at :288-289) + run_command_with_timeout (src/chat_command/executor.rs, unbounded join at :194-195). The group kill already existed (setpgid pre_exec + killpg); the hole is the join, on BOTH paths: plain (sh exits immediately, no timeout fires) and timeout (setsid escapes the kill). Repro: `sleep 30 &` and `setsid sleep 30 & sleep 30` with a 2s timeout. On unhardened code all 4 regression tests fail (call blocks ~30s until the orphaned sleep dies on its own, past the 10s bound). 385.2 IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-24 (branch ranger-helix-h9): new join_drain helper in both files (DRAIN_JOIN_GRACE 2s, is_finished() poll every 10ms, detach the JoinHandle on expiry); run_shell surfaces abandonment with a [notice: a background child still holds the output pipes] line; the chat-command path folds abandonment into the existing truncation flags so the reply renders [truncated]; no ExecutionOutcome struct change. Windows Job Object out of scope; non-Unix child.kill() fallback unchanged. Known limit (same as the H10 evaluator precedent): bytes already read into the abandoned thread's local buffer are dropped, so an abandoned stream comes back empty rather than partial. 385.3 VERIFY: 4 new regression tests (2 per path: plain background child + timeout-path setsid escape) confirmed FAILING on unhardened code first (30.01s) and passing after (6.03s).
